author: blu
body: A single loop that holds many client connections at once and never serves one to completion before looking at the next. It polls the NIC once per turn and dispatches the frame to the connection that owns it -- by (local port, remote port), the same demultiplex the stack uses. Because the NE2K RX ring buffers inbound frames and this one loop is the only reader of every connection, a request for connection B that arrives while A is mid-flight waits in the ring and is delivered to B when the loop next polls; it is never read by the wrong connection's loop and dropped. That is the concurrency guarantee -- a server holds more than one connection without losing requests -- and it needs no per-session parking, because there is exactly one reader.

author: blu
body: Each connection accumulates its incoming bytes until a full HTTP request is present -- headers terminated by a blank line, plus any Content-Length body -- and only then parses and answers it, draining pipelined requests in one pass and keeping any partial tail for the next frame. So a request split across frames, a header set larger than one segment, or a POST body all arrive whole. The client's GET usually rides in on the ACK that completes the handshake (PSH+ACK); the TCP SYN_RECEIVED path delivers that payload rather than dropping it, so no retransmit is needed.
